sentences.text: Protitanichthys is an extinct genus of large arthrodire placoderms, a class of armored fish.
Its classification places it in the clade Coccosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci, though the Paleobi Database assigns it to the family Panxiosteidae instead of Coccosteidae.
While resembling other coccosteids, this animal possessed a proportionally narrower skull and smaller eye orbits, making it the second-largest known coccosteid after Livosteus.
Most known specimens measure about 0.5 meters long, although rare fossils exceed 2 meters.
The type species was described based on a cranial roof approximately 20 cm long.
The genus was first described by Eastman in 1907.
Many fragmented remains of the species Protitanichthys rockportensis have been found in Michigan.
Protitanichthys lived between 393.47 and 382.31 million years ago, specifically from the Eifelian to the Lower Givetian stages.
Fossils of this animal are found in the Delaware Limestone of Ohio and the Rockport Quarry Limestone of Michigan.
It is debated whether Protitanichthys rockportensis is a distinct species from P. fossatus, as differences are limited to time and location.
